summary: Router 0.19.0 (same unreleased v0.26.0 as ADR-0052): the control port requires users even on loopback (ADR-0053, TM-02). auth.basic_auth_middleware no longer serves loopback peers without users unless control_auth.allow_unauthenticated_loopback is the boolean true, the listener is literal 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and the peer is loopback; otherwise 503 before any handler or CSRF check. config validates the switch as a boolean (schema entry added) and app logs a start warning whenever no control users exist. The /v1/ tunnel path keeps its own Ed25519 authentication and is untouched. Breaking only for password-free development setups; the reference deployment configures control users and TLS. Rebased onto main after #90 and #93; German texts follow main's spelling.

findings.evidence: router 0.18.x auth.basic_auth_middleware served any loopback peer on a loopback listener without users, which a local reverse proxy also is.
findings.resolution: Fixed: explicit boolean development switch required (auth.py, config.py, app.py warning); selftest_security covers a proxy-like loopback peer, the switch, a remote peer and a non-loopback listener; the check fails against the previous middleware.

tests.evidence: PASS loopback without users is denied unless explicitly allowed; PASS explicit development switch allows unauthenticated loopback; PASS development switch never opens the port to other addresses; PASS development switch needs a literal loopback listener.

tests.command: Negative check (before rebase): selftest_security.py against the previous middleware
tests.evidence: AttributeError at 'loopback without users is denied unless explicitly allowed': the old middleware returned the handler result.
PASS control_auth.allow_unauthenticated_loopback defaults to false; PASS invalid (allow_unauthenticated_loopback not boolean): Problem.

tests.command: Every `python test/...` and `python router/...` command of the router CI job (ci.yml), except integration/e2e; ruff check .; check_adr_index.py
tests.evidence: No failures; All checks passed; ADR index ok: 53 ADRs; router.py --check config.example.yaml --pure: configuration ok.

limitations: A real reverse-proxy topology is not exercised in CI; the unit tests model its loopback peer.
PostgreSQL session-store integration and the nightly end-to-end suite were not run locally; CI runs the PostgreSQL job.
